proposal: The Mandate recommends a comprehensive cost-benefit review of US participation in all international organizations, withholding funds from those that conflict with US interests or promote policies it opposes, and serious consideration of withdrawal from organizations that no longer have value. It cites the first Trump term's exits or funding cuts for the UN Human Rights Council, UNESCO, UNRWA and the WHO as a model, and calls for tighter restrictions on WHO and other health-body funding.

status_summary: Executive Order 14155 (signed 2025-01-20) began the WHO withdrawal and paused transfers of funds, and HHS and the State Department announced the withdrawal complete on 2026-01-22. Executive Order 14199 (signed 2025-02-04) ended US participation in the UN Human Rights Council, ended funding for UNRWA, ordered a 90-day UNESCO membership review and ordered a 180-day review of all international organizations and treaties. A State Department statement of 2025-07-22, read through third-party copies, announced a UNESCO exit effective 2026-12-31. The Rescissions Act of 2025 (Public Law 119-28) rescinded unobligated balances in several international organization accounts. A presidential memorandum signed 2026-01-07 directed agencies to withdraw from 66 organizations (31 UN entities and 35 others), including the UNFCCC, the IPCC, UN Women and UNFPA, and said review of further findings was continuing; the UN depositary recorded the UNFCCC withdrawal notice on 2026-02-27, effective 2027-02-27. The Mandate recommended a review and serious consideration of withdrawal; the 2026 memorandum covers 66 bodies at once, including climate and gender bodies the Mandate did not name.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14155 stated the US intends to withdraw from the WHO, directed a pause in transfers of funds and resources, recall of US personnel working with the WHO, and a halt to negotiation of the WHO Pandemic Agreement (published in the Federal Register 2025-01-29).

Executive Order 14199 ended US participation in the UN Human Rights Council, barred funding to UNRWA, ordered a 90-day review of UNESCO membership, and ordered a 180-day State Department review of all international organizations and treaties with recommendations on withdrawal (published 2025-02-10).

The State Department announces the US will withdraw from UNESCO under Article II(6) of the UNESCO constitution, effective 2026-12-31, with the US a full member until then (statement read through third-party copies); the exit is not yet effective as of 2026-10-12.
timeline.source: State Department statement (copy hosted by Poder360)

timeline.event: The Rescissions Act of 2025 (Public Law 119-28) rescinded unobligated balances in international organization accounts, including about $202 million in Contributions to International Organizations, about $361 million in peacekeeping contributions and about $437 million in International Organizations and Programs.

A presidential memorandum directed agencies to take immediate steps to withdraw from 66 organizations (31 UN entities and 35 non-UN bodies), ending participation and, for UN entities, funding to the extent permitted by law; it set no deadline and said review of further findings was ongoing (published 2026-01-16).
JURIST reported the memorandum and the UN climate chief's reaction calling the move a mistake and noting the door remains open to rejoin; no legal challenge was reported in the article.

HHS and the State Department announce the US has completed its WHO withdrawal, one year after Executive Order 14155; the release says the US stopped WHO funding and withdrew personnel during the year and will coordinate with the WHO only in a limited way to finish the exit.
The UN Secretary-General, as depositary, records the US notification of withdrawal from the UNFCCC, which takes effect for the US on 2027-02-27, one year after receipt.

uncertainties: The UNESCO effective date rests on the State Department statement as reproduced by two third-party hosts (Poder360 and GlobalSecurity.org), which agree; the official page was not opened. Effective dates for exits other than WHO, UNESCO and UNFCCC were not verified. The outcome of the 90-day UNESCO review and the 180-day review report were not located. Geneva Consensus Declaration status and UN dues payments were not verified. The fact sheet was read as a third-party copy of a White House document. Rescissions Act dollar figures are summed from account-level amounts (an inference). A limited search found no lawsuit or new withdrawal tranche after February 2026; an E&E News report of 2026-01-20 described legal debate but no filed case. A news report that the WHO cites unpaid US contributions was not carried forward because it was not checked against a primary source.
